recommendation: Keep this audit commit as-is. Revisit only if the Vocabulary/Terminology Infrastructure work group opens a new final issue to add a distinct server-version element beyond the existing CapabilityStatement-style model.
issue_request: FHIR-14552 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It asked for TerminologyCapabilities to identify the server it describes, for example by reference to CapabilityStatement.url and CapabilityStatement.version, and the resolution said to add server .url, .version, and .description based on CapabilityStatement.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied in svn revision 14629, represented in git as ecf37e5e12a995d95d0e549e90a8aa32e6d83a2a (#GF14552 - add to TerminologyCapabilities). That commit added the CapabilityStatement-style kind, software.name/version, and implementation.description/url structure to the TerminologyCapabilities spreadsheet and example. The current source preserves the same model in the active TerminologyCapabilities StructureDefinition.
additional_context: TerminologyCapabilities is active in source/fhir.ini and marked normative. CapabilityStatement itself uses the same software.version plus implementation.description/url separation rather than an implementation.version element. Later Published issue FHIR-24698 updated terminology service CapabilityStatement/TerminologyCapabilities examples and required terminology metadata without adding a distinct server or implementation version element. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later final decision requiring such an element.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Adding TerminologyCapabilities.server.version or TerminologyCapabilities.implementation.version now would introduce new normative content not supported by the applied source history or later related requirements.

related_jiras.note: Later Published terminology service capability issue updated examples and minimum terminology capabilities expectations without requiring a distinct server or implementation version element.
